study type: Comparative analysis of national cross-sectional surveys and routine data
exposure: Birth during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020 vs 2018)
cohort: Women who participated in national maternity surveys in England in 2018 (pre-pandemic, n=4,509) and 2020 (during the pandemic, n=4,611).
finding: Breastfeeding initiation and any breastfeeding at 6 weeks in England were largely unaffected by the pandemic, while birth during the pandemic was associated with a 3 percentage point decrease in EBF at 6 weeks but a 3 percentage point increase in any breastfeeding at 6 months, with persistent inequalities observed across groups.
cross-section timing: Surveys conducted in 2018 (pre-pandemic) and 2020 (during the pandemic), interpreted in context of routine data from 2009-10 to 2020-21.
